title: Job search intake, version 1
description: A person's answers to the setup questions. Produced by the setup page (or written by hand) and read by generate_project.py --intake. Free text is copied into the tracker's files word for word. 'title' is the question as the page asks it; 'description' is the one-line reason shown under it; 'x-labels' are the words shown for each choice.

job_finder.title: Turn on the assistant that finds roles for you
job_finder.description: It searches public job boards and lists matches for you to review. It never applies for you.

drafting.title: Draft cover letters for good matches
drafting.description: Drafts are for you to review and send yourself. Needs the job finder.

priorities.title: Rank what matters most to you in your next job (top 3)
priorities.description: Every offer is a trade. Knowing your order ahead of time makes the choice clearer when an offer arrives.

tradeoff.title: What would you give up to get your #1?
tradeoff.description: For example: some pay for fully remote, or a bigger title for a more stable company.

pay_floor.title: The lowest base pay you would accept
pay_floor.description: Decide this before you talk to anyone. It's much harder to set during a conversation with a recruiter.

pay_other.title: Which other parts of the package matter to you?
pay_other.description: Base pay is only part of an offer. Two offers with the same base can be very different.

pay_notes.title: Anything else about pay
pay_notes.description: For example: why this number, or what equity is worth to you.

balance.title: Hours, on-call and travel: what are your limits?
balance.description: Easier to decide now than to discover after you start.

work_arrangements.title: Which ways of working are you open to?

locations.title: Where can you work, and how far will you commute?

company_size.title: What size of company do you want?
company_size.description: Smaller usually means more scope and more risk; larger usually means more structure and more stability. Leave it empty for no preference.

timeline.title: How long can you search before pressure starts making the choice for you?
timeline.description: Knowing this helps you see when you're saying yes to a role because it's right, and when it's because time is running out.

dealbreakers.title: Dealbreakers: what would make you say no even if the pay is great?

work_authorization.description: Optional. Stays on your computer. Used to skip roles that can't hire you and to keep your deadlines in view. General information only, not legal advice.

x-labels.no_sponsorship_needed: I don't need sponsorship (citizen or green card)
x-labels.dependent_ead: EAD as a dependent (e.g. H-4, L-2)

authorized_until.title: When does your current authorization end?
authorized_until.description: Claude keeps this date in view and checks in as it gets closer.

x-labels.new_h1b: A new H-1B (this goes through the lottery)
x-labels.e_verify_employer: An E-Verify employer (needed for STEM OPT)

needs.title: What do you need from an employer?

green_card_timing.title: When do you need green card sponsorship to start?

notes.title: Anything else about your situation
notes.description: For example: a grace period you're in, or a spouse's status that depends on yours.

risk.description: Optional. Helps weigh stability against upside. Stays on your computer.

x-labels.high: High: I can take a chance

comfort.title: How much risk can you take on right now?

runway.title: How long could you cover your costs without a job?

dependents.title: Does anyone depend on your income?

layoff_impact.title: If you were laid off six months into a new job, what would that mean for you?
layoff_impact.description: There's no wrong answer. It helps judge how much a company's stability matters to you.

titles.title: Job titles to look for
titles.description: One per line, as they appear in job postings, e.g. “Senior data analyst”.

sources.title: Where should it look?
sources.description: It reads these straight from their public listings. You can change this any time.

x-help.company_boards: Many companies post here first, and it checks the company's own board directly.
x-help.yc: Startups funded by Y Combinator, often small and early.
x-help.hn: A monthly thread where companies post roles; some invite you to email the hiring manager directly.
x-help.web: Finds roles anywhere, but results can be out of date, so it checks the company's own page before trusting them.

run_size.title: How much should it do each run?
run_size.description: Bigger runs find more and use more of your Claude usage.

x-labels.thorough: Thorough: more searching and more reading

x-labels.strong_and_maybe: Strong matches, plus maybes with one clear gap

drafts.title: What should it draft for you on its own?
drafts.description: Drafts are always for you to review and send yourself.

x-labels.none: Nothing; I'll ask when I want one
x-labels.strong_with_outreach: Cover letters, plus short emails when a posting invites you to write directly

watch_companies.title: Companies to check on every run
watch_companies.description: One per line. Their job boards are checked directly each time.

daily_run.title: When should the job finder run each day?
daily_run.description: It searches while you're away and has new matches waiting for you. Each run uses some of your Claude usage; it skips the day when plenty is already waiting for your review. Choose a time (24-hour, default 08:00) or off. You can change it any time.

strengths.title: In a few sentences, what are you good at?
strengths.description: In your own words. Claude uses this together with your resume.

links.title: Links
links.description: One per line: a portfolio, a public profile, a personal site.

voice_sample.title: Something you wrote that sounds like you
voice_sample.description: Optional. A past cover letter or email you liked; drafts will follow its tone.

stories.description: Optional. A useful answer has the moment, your part (say 'I', not only 'we': interviewers need to know what you did), a choice you made and why, and what changed. A few honest sentences beat a polished paragraph.

x-labels.hard_call: A hard call you made in your work
x-labels.saw_differently: A time you and a colleague saw a problem differently
x-labels.no_clear_answer: A time you had to decide without a clear answer
x-labels.moved_people: A time you got people moving in one direction without being their manager
x-labels.not_as_planned: Something that didn't go as planned, and what you did next
x-labels.beyond_the_ask: A time you did more than you were asked, and why
x-labels.other: A story you want to tell
